newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary approves law to aid Holocaust survivors.
newsitem.headline: Hungary approves law to aid Holocaust survivors.

text.p: The Hungarian parliament has passed a law to compensate Jewish survivors of the Holocaust, newspapers and radio reported on Wednesday.

The parliament authorised the government to make available four billion forints ($24 million) in compensation coupons that would be administered by a public foundation to aid the Jewish community, the reports said.
Life annuities may be claimed by Hungarian Jews who are over 60 and are permanent residents, the reports said.
There are believed to be about 10,000 to 15,000 elderly Holocaust survivors living in Hungary, which has a total Jewish community of 80,000 to 100,000, compared with 800,000 before World War Two.
The compensation coupons entitle the owners to buy land or shares in government-owned businesses.

The programme is to be administered by a public foundation which must be approved by another act of parliament. The membership of the foundation's 21-person board has been agreed after lengthy negotiations involving the government, the Hungarian Jewish community and the World Jewish Congress.

The law passed by parliament implements an article of the Paris Peace Treaty of 1947 under which property confiscated by the fascists for racial or religious reasons and unclaimed by inheritors after the war must be turned over to organisations of the communities concerned.
The money is to be spent to support the communities and family members still living, the news reports said. It was not immediately possible to confirm the reports.
